badge.name: Checked Twice, Not Once
badge.note: Every defect found before the engine started, the stop sequence run in order, the danger zone scanned before the door opened, and the mirrors checked again before the bus ever moved off the curb

badges.note: Checked the mirrors before pulling out and again before releasing the brake at the stop

badges.name: Never a Shortcut
badges.note: No defect ignored, no phone touched, nobody moved without a full stop and a scan first

badges.name: Clean Run
badges.note: No corrections anywhere in the run

challenges.name: Yard Out on Time
challenges.note: Walkaround and cab setup finished inside 80% of par

challenges.name: One-Pass Walkaround
challenges.note: Pre-trip walkaround clean on the first pass

challenges.name: Ten in a Row
challenges.note: Ten correct actions in a row

hazards.cross-in-front-close: That student is inside the danger zone right at the front bumper, and the bus has not been cleared to move. The zone around a school bus is the one stretch of ground the driver cannot see well from the seat — it gets scanned and cleared before the bus goes anywhere, not assumed clear because the mirrors looked fine a moment ago.
hazards.loose-strap-hanging: A backpack strap is hanging out of the closed door. A strap caught in a door that then pulls away drags whoever is wearing it alongside the bus — the door does not count as clear until nothing is hanging out of it.
hazards.phone-lit-on-dash: The phone on the dash just lit up during loading. Every second spent looking at it during boarding is a second the mirrors and the danger zone are not being watched, and boarding is exactly when a student is most likely to dart out from between the bus and the curb.
hazards.walk-behind-bus: That student is walking behind the bus instead of coming around where the driver can actually see them. The rear of a school bus is one more blind stretch on top of the danger zone at the front — the loading procedure exists to keep every student on the side and at the distance the driver's mirrors can actually cover.

interrupts.alert: A student who missed the first call is sprinting from behind a parked car toward the bus, outside the crosswalk and not visible until now.
interrupts.cue: Sound the horn — don't wave them across yet.
interrupts.kind: Late student runs from behind a parked car
interrupts.missNote: The student kept running straight into the danger zone with nobody's attention on them — a late arrival outside the crosswalk is exactly the student this stop's whole procedure is built to catch before they reach the bus, not after.
interrupts.why: A horn is the fastest way to make a running student stop and look before they close the last few feet into the danger zone, and it is sounded before anyone is waved forward — the loading procedure does not resume until the student is stopped and accounted for, not just noticed.
interrupts.wrongNote: The horn — that's what stops a running student before they close the distance, not a wave or a shout.

interrupts.alert: Right as the bus starts to roll, a small figure that was crouched out of mirror view at the front bumper suddenly stands up.
interrupts.kind: Someone stands up at the front bumper as the bus starts to move
interrupts.missNote: The bus kept rolling with someone right at the bumper who had just stood up out of nowhere — a school bus that keeps moving through that is the collision the whole loading procedure exists to prevent.
interrupts.why: A figure below mirror height at the bumper is invisible until they move, and the only safe response to seeing one appear the instant the bus starts moving is a full stop, not a slow-down — this is exactly the moment the second mirror check earlier in the stop was meant to prevent, and it still needs an immediate stop now that it's happened.
interrupts.wrongNote: The brake — stop the bus now, before anything else.

lateNotes.brake-pedal: The full stop happens once the bus is actually at the marked curb spot, not before.
lateNotes.light-switch: Not yet — the amber lights go on approaching the stop, not while the bus is still moving through the route.

name: Bus Pre-Trip & Loading Zone

passRule.note: stars >= 2 and no unsafe action (WebXR/shared/records.js passed())

steps.cue: Read the route board for today's stop order, student count and any noted needs.
steps.prompt: Read the route board for today's stop order, student count and any noted needs.
steps.title: Read this morning's run sheet
steps.why: The run sheet is where a driver learns who to expect at which stop and what today's route changes are before ever starting the engine — a stop skipped or a student missed because the sheet was never read is a call home the district has to make, not a surprise the road should be producing.

steps.cue: Three things about this bus are not right. Find them before the key turns.

itemNames.brake-light-out: the warning lamp that doesn't light
itemNames.worn-tire: the tyre worn to its wear bar

itemNotes.brake-light-out: One of the eight warning lamps doesn't light when tested. A driver behind who never sees that lamp never gets the warning it's built to give, and this bus doesn't roll on a route until it's replaced.
itemNotes.cracked-mirror: The crossview mirror is cracked across one corner. That mirror is what shows the ground right in front of the bumper — cracked, it hides exactly the part of the danger zone a driver can least afford to lose.
itemNotes.worn-tire: This tyre is worn flush with its wear bar. A tyre at that point stops shedding water the way the tread pattern is designed to, which shows up first as a longer stopping distance in the rain — exactly the condition a loaded school bus can least afford.

steps.prompt: Three things about this bus are not right. Find them before the key turns.
steps.title: Walk round the bus before the engine starts
steps.why: 49 CFR 396 puts the pre-trip walkaround before the engine starts for a reason: every one of these three defects is easiest to find with the bus sitting still and silent, and hardest to notice once it's already moving with a load of students aboard.

steps.cue: Belt on, then set every mirror to show the danger zone around the bus, then read the gauges before moving.

itemNames.mirrors-adjusted: mirrors set to show the danger zone

steps.outOfOrderNote: Belt first, then the mirrors, then the gauges — mirrors are set from the belted driving position, not before it.
steps.prompt: Belt on, then set every mirror to show the danger zone around the bus, then read the gauges before moving.
steps.title: Belt, mirrors, gauges
steps.why: The belt goes on first because the yard and the road ahead both start the moment the bus moves; the mirrors are set from the seat the driver will actually be sitting in, aimed at the ground around the bus rather than the horizon, because that ground is what the whole loading procedure depends on being able to see.

steps.cue: Watch the gauges come up to normal operating range and commit the reading before pulling out.

gauge.label: GAUGES
gauge.missNote: Not settled in the normal band yet. Give the gauges time to come up, or flag what isn't reading right, before pulling out.

steps.prompt: Watch the gauges come up to normal operating range and commit the reading before pulling out.
steps.title: Read the gauges to normal operating range
steps.why: A gauge that never settles into its normal band is telling the driver something the walkaround on the ground could not — low air, low oil pressure, an overheating engine — and it gets read and committed before the bus leaves the yard, not glanced at once it's already rolling.

steps.cue: Check the mirrors, signal, and pull out past the blind driveway toward the marked stop.

drive.bandLabel: yard speed, per the posted limit

checks.note: Left mirror before moving — the yard behind the bus is exactly where another bus backs out.
Signal before the driveway, so anything on the street already knows the bus is coming out.
The driveway to the street is blind past the fence line — the horn is what warns anyone already on the other side of it.
Right mirror as the bus settles onto the street — the curb side is where the stop is coming up.

drive.laneNote: The bus left the lane and stayed out — on a yard driveway that is either the fence line or oncoming traffic on the street.

steps.holdBreakNote: Out of the lane or out of the band pulling out. Hold the lane at yard speed and check the mirrors before committing to the driveway.
steps.prompt: Check the mirrors, signal, and pull out past the blind driveway toward the marked stop.
steps.title: Pull out of the yard toward the stop
steps.why: The yard's own driveway is blind from the seat until the nose of the bus is already past the fence line, which is exactly why the mirrors are checked before moving and the horn is tapped crossing it — a habit built here in the empty yard is the same habit that has to hold on every blind driveway the whole route passes.

steps.cue: Approaching the stop, switch the amber warning lights on before slowing.
steps.prompt: Approaching the stop, switch the amber warning lights on before slowing.
steps.title: Switch on the amber warning lights
steps.why: The amber lights come on first, ahead of the red lights and the stop arm, precisely so traffic behind has warning the bus is about to stop before it actually does — a driver who only sees the red lights and the stop arm at the same moment the bus stops has already lost the warning the amber phase exists to give them.

steps.cue: Hold the brake until the bus is fully stopped at the curb's marked spot.
steps.holdBreakNote: The brake eased off before the bus was fully stopped. The stop sequence starts from a dead stop at the marked spot, not from still slowing down.
steps.prompt: Hold the brake until the bus is fully stopped at the curb's marked spot.
steps.title: Bring the bus to a full stop at the marked spot
steps.why: Nothing about the loading procedure — the stop arm, the crossing gate, the door — happens until the bus is actually stopped, not slowing down to a stop; a stop arm deployed while the bus is still rolling tells the traffic behind a story that isn't true yet.

steps.cue: Pull the lever to swing out the stop arm, the red lights and the crossing gate together.
steps.prompt: Pull the lever to swing out the stop arm, the red lights and the crossing gate together.
steps.title: Deploy the stop arm and crossing gate
steps.why: The stop arm tells traffic to stop, the crossing gate keeps a student from cutting across the road right in front of the bumper where the driver can least see them, and both come out together because a stop arm without the gate still leaves the shortest, least visible path across the street wide open.

steps.cue: Open the door once the stop arm and crossing gate are fully out.
steps.prompt: Open the door once the stop arm and crossing gate are fully out.
steps.title: Open the door
steps.why: The door opens after the stop arm and gate, not before, because a door open onto a street that isn't yet actually stopped for is an invitation to step out into traffic that hasn't been told to stop yet.

steps.cue: Three things in the danger zone need catching before boarding starts. Find them in the mirrors.

itemNames.dropped-backpack: the backpack dropped right at the front bumper
itemNames.student-crossing-behind: the student heading around the back of the bus
itemNames.student-tying-shoe: the student crouched at the bumper

itemNotes.dropped-backpack: A backpack has been dropped directly in the danger zone at the front bumper. Anyone about to reach for it is standing exactly where the driver's own sightline cannot reach.
itemNotes.student-crossing-behind: A student is walking around the back of the bus instead of the front where the crossing gate and the driver's attention are both aimed.
itemNotes.student-tying-shoe: A student has crouched down at the front bumper to tie a shoe, low enough that they've dropped below where the mirrors show anything at all.

steps.prompt: Three things in the danger zone need catching before boarding starts. Find them in the mirrors.
steps.title: Scan the danger zone before waving anyone forward
steps.why: The ground around a school bus has more blind area than clear area from the driver's seat, and the mirrors are the only tool that covers most of it — this scan happens every single stop, not just the ones where something looks obviously wrong, because the two or three feet right at the bumper look the same whether they're empty or not.

steps.cue: Confirm the door area is clear, count students aboard against the run sheet, then confirm everyone is seated.
steps.outOfOrderNote: Clear, then count, then seated — the count only means something once the door area is confirmed clear of stragglers first.
steps.prompt: Confirm the door area is clear, count students aboard against the run sheet, then confirm everyone is seated.
steps.title: Load and count the students aboard
steps.why: The count against the run sheet is what tells the driver the stop is actually finished — a door closed on an assumption instead of a confirmed count is how a district ends up with a student who never made it onto a bus that already left the curb.

steps.cue: Close the door once every student is seated and counted.
steps.prompt: Close the door once every student is seated and counted.
steps.title: Close the door
steps.why: The door closes last in the sequence for the same reason it opened last going in — it is the one thing standing between the aisle and the street, and it stays open exactly as long as the boarding it was opened for is still happening.

steps.cue: Check both mirrors and the danger zone once more, then pull away from the curb.

checks.note: Right mirror one more time before the bus actually starts moving — the curb side is exactly where a late student reappears.
Left mirror as the bus pulls away from the curb — anything passing on the left is now closing on a bus that's moving again.
Signal back into the travel lane so the traffic behind knows the stop is over.

steps.holdBreakNote: Out of lane or band pulling away from the curb — settle the bus into the lane before building speed.
steps.prompt: Check both mirrors and the danger zone once more, then pull away from the curb.
steps.title: Check the mirrors again before pulling away
steps.why: The collision this whole stop is built to prevent happens most often after the stop arm is already back in and the bus is moving again — a student who darted out from behind a parked car during loading and is still crossing when the bus starts to roll is invisible to a driver who checked the mirrors only once, at the start of the stop.

steps.cue: Record the walkaround defects and the stop on the inspection report before the next stop.
steps.prompt: Record the walkaround defects and the stop on the inspection report before the next stop.
steps.title: Log the pre-trip and the stop
steps.why: The inspection report is the district's record of what was found and fixed before this bus ever carried a student today — a worn tyre or a dead warning lamp that isn't written down is a defect the shop has no way of knowing to fix before tomorrow's run.

supportLine: your AFT or CSEA chapter's member assistance line, or the district's employee assistance programme
tagline: First light in the yard: the walkaround before the engine turns over, a short pull-out to the curb, amber lights before the stop, a full stop, the stop arm and crossing gate out together, the danger zone scanned in the mirrors, students counted aboard, the door shut, and the mirrors checked again before the bus ever rolls
